scenes.headline: How an old executable gives away its build machine
scenes.sub: Bitcoin's first Windows release, rebuilt from source to the same hash
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Keel! In 2009 Satoshi shipped a Windows program with its source. This year someone rebuilt it, byte for byte.

scenes.text: A hash match leaves nothing to chance: the compiler, two linkers, the libraries, the shell and three clock readings all had to be recovered from the file itself.
scenes.say: One wrong byte gives a different hash. So the compiler, the linkers, the libraries, the shell and even the clock had to be read back out of the old file.

steps.say: First the libraries. wxWidgets and Berkeley DB were built in November, with an older binutils.
Then binutils was upgraded. Bitcoin's own files were compiled as a debug build, with full optimisation only on the hashing file.
Windres packed the icons and the manifest, and stamped every resource folder with the time it ran.
Last, strip removed the symbols and wrote its own time into the header. That file is what shipped.

scenes.title: Where the clues sit in the file

steps.say: The header says GNU ld, not Microsoft's linker. There is no Rich header at all.
In the code, import stubs sit eight bytes apart. The repository ties that to the newer binutils.
The strings name gcc three point four point five, and keep include paths that only a plain command window would leave alone.
The resources carry seventy nine time stamps, and a manifest with Windows line endings.

scenes.label: differ if the three clock readings are left real
scenes.note: header stamp, resource stamps, one date and time string

steps.say: The target is the hash of the released file, six point four megabytes. The rebuild prints match only when it is reached.

scenes.text: A build that pins its toolchain and fixes its clock is reproducible by design. This one had to be reproduced backwards.

recap: Every byte comes from source, tools or clock
The binary names its compiler, linkers and shell
Fixed clocks close the last gap
scenes.say: Source, tools and clock. Get all three, and the hash follows.
